{"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":44197,"items":[{"DOI":"10.2139/ssrn.5807626","title":["Open-Set Domain Generalization through Spectral-Spatial Uncertainty Disentanglement for Hyperspectral Image Classification"],"author":[{"given":"Amirreza","family":"Khoshbakht","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]},{"given":"Erchan","family":"Aptoula","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025]]},"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5807626","type":"posted-content"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Domain Adaptation (DA) and Domain Generalization (DG) are critical towards designing efficient image classification and face recognition systems that can be practical with distribution shifts to real-life settings. Although supervised deep learning models achieve strong performance under matched training and test conditions their accuracy often degrades significantly when exposed to variations in illumination, pose, sensor characteristics, background context, demographic attributes and environmental conditions. To address these challenges a wide range of DA and DG methods have been proposed to align feature distributions, learn invariant representations and improve generalization under unseen domains. This review presents a unified and systematic analysis of DA and DG techniques for image classification and face recognition. We first summarize the fundamental principles of distribution shift and outline the limitations of conventional supervised learning. Major DA paradigms including adversarial alignment, discrepancy minimization, generative translation, clustering-based adaptation and source-free adaptation are reviewed and compared in terms of their assumptions, strengths and limitations. In parallel, DG strategies such as invariant risk minimization, style randomization, meta-learning and multimodal robustness are discussed for scenarios where target-domain data are unavailable. The review highlights real-world applications and analyzes open challenges related to pseudo-label noise, over-alignment, fairness, privacy and adversarial domain shifts. Finally, emerging research directions including foundation-model adaptation, diffusion-based synthesis, causal representation learning, federated learning and test-time or source-free adaptation are identified.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.36227/techrxiv.176652489.98163771/v1","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Systematic Review of Domain Adaptation and Generalization in Image Classification and Face Recognition"],"author":[{"given":"Sundas","family":"Iqbal","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4828-4239","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Danish","family":"Ali","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Qing","family":"Tian","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,12,23]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.176652489.98163771/v1"},{"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Current machine learning methods for medical image analysis primarily focus on developing models tailored for their specific tasks, utilizing data within their target domain. These specialized models tend to be data-hungry and often exhibit limitations in generalizing to out-of-distribution samples. In this work, we show that employing models that incorporate multiple domains instead of specialized ones significantly alleviates the limitations observed in specialized models. We refer to this approach as
                    <jats:italic>multi-domain model</jats:italic>
                    and compare its performance to that of specialized models. For this, we introduce the incorporation of diverse medical image domains, including different imaging modalities like X-ray, MRI, CT, and ultrasound images, as well as various viewpoints such as axial, coronal, and sagittal views. Our findings underscore the superior generalization capabilities of multi-domain models, particularly in scenarios characterized by limited data availability and out-of-distribution, frequently encountered in healthcare applications. The integration of diverse data allows multi-domain models to utilize information across domains, enhancing the overall outcomes substantially. To illustrate, for organ recognition, multi-domain model can enhance accuracy by up to 8% compared to conventional specialized models.

Visual Computer"],"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.1007/s00371-025-04338-1","type":"journal-article"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Feature alignment domain adaptation (DA) methods such as CORAL and MMD are widely used to mitigate distribution shift between training (source) and deployment (target) domains. They are typically evaluated on a single downstream classifier, which implicitly assumes that the alignment benefit transfers across model families. We test this assumption on a controlled class-symmetric shift of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope features, with five carrier classifiers, three alignment methods, and fifteen seeds per cell. Establishing this requires first correcting an evaluation protocol that we believe to be common in benchmarks built by perturbing a single sample: when the target consist of a perturbed copy of data that the carrier was partly trained on, the measured benefit of adaptation is inflated by a factor that tracks the carrier’s capacity to memorise (from 1.0 for logistic regression to 5.7 for an unbounded-depth random forest), so that such a benchmark reports a carrier gradient whether or not one actually exists. When scored only on events that no carrier has seen, the carrier still matters (indeed, twice over): the same shift costs a hyperplane carrier 0.004 of AUC and a tree ensemble 0.006–0.008, and CORAL then recovers 58% of that loss on logistic regression, against 84–98% on the tree ensembles, a difference that RBF-kernel MMD does not show on any carrier for which the ratio is determined. A measurement of marginal sensitivity taken without any adaptation reproduces the ordering. Two effects that would be reported by a full-target protocol are absent on held-out events: a benefit growing with tree depth, and an advantage of covariance alignment over mean matching on deep trees. We propose a two-axis framework (shift symmetry × carrier marginal sensitivity), then test its class-symmetric row and give practical recommendations for evaluating and deploying domain adaptation under shift.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.3390/a19100859","type":"journal-article","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["When Feature Alignment Helps, Hurts, or Washes out: Carrier-Dependent Domain Adaptation for Cherenkov Telescope Event Classification"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6841-1362","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Antonio","family":"Pagliaro","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"INAF—Istituto di Astrofisica Spaziale e Fisica Cosmica di Palermo, Via Ugo La Malfa 153, I-90146 Palermo, Italy"},{"name":"Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare Sezione di Catania, Via Santa Sofia, 64, I-95123 Catania, Italy"},{"name":"ICSC—Centro Nazionale di Ricerca in HPC, Big Data e Quantum Computing, I-40121 Bologna, Italy"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"container-title":["Algorithms"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,9]]},"URL":"https://doi.org/10.3390/a19100859"},{"DOI":"10.1117/12.3054360","title":["Predictive measures of out-of-distribution generalization"],"author":[{"given":"Daniel","family":"Cho","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]},{"given":"Christopher","family":"Ebersole","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]},{"given":"Edmund","family":"Zelnio","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,5,28]]},"container-title":["Algorithms for Synthetic Aperture Radar Imagery XXXII"],"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https://doi.org/10.1117/12.3054360","type":"proceedings-article"}],"items-per-page":10,"query":{"start-index":0,"search-terms":null}}}
